items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: at the Job Corps, I played for the Job Corps one time and there was this young comedian who was also playing there, a guy named Richard Pryor.

ctx.x: Wow. And were you performing — mostly that would have been as a solo performer.

Oh yeah. Most of my career has been solo. I love, as you probably found out, I love playing with other people, but mostly I play by myself. And I did play some in Chicago but I played for nothing. I played for the Job Corps Center, I played for veterans’ hospitals, this was when the Vietnam War was going on and there were a lot of paraplegics, you know I played for them. You know, great audience. But at the Job Corps, I played for the Job Corps one time and there was this young comedian who was also playing…
And this would have been the early seventies?
